children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after Nvidia shares pulled back from the previous session's rally amid lingering corporate governance concerns and warnings of continued scrutiny.

CNBC reported that Nvidia shares tumbled around 7%, paring gains after soaring more than 30% in the previous session following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. According to the report, other U.S. semiconductor stocks also opened lower after strong previous-session gains, with Micron and AMD plunging 10% and Marvell Technology and Arm Holdings tumbling 8% in morning trading.

Analysts warned that scrutiny of Nvidia would continue, the report said. Strategy Asset Managers CEO Tom Hulick told CNBC that Nvidia still has "a lot of things to worry about" regarding corporate governance.

When a dominant industry leader pulls back after a sharp rebound, investors often reassess valuations and governance risks across related stocks. Share prices across a sector frequently decline together when doubts about customer spending and sector catalysts persist.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Texas Instruments’s shares are quite volatile and have had 15 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock gained 10% on the news that Cantor Fitzgerald upgraded the stock to Overweight from Neutral and raised its price target to $385 from $340, amid a broader rally in semiconductor stocks. CNBC reported that Cantor Fitzgerald made the upgrade after meeting with Texas Instruments' management, saying it was impressed and reiterating a bullish stance on analog chips. CNBC separately reported that broader U.S. equities and chipmakers surged after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, reviving the artificial intelligence trade. According to that report, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF rose more than 16%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite soared 5.1% and 6.9%, respectively.

Texas Instruments is up 47.2% since the beginning of the year, but at $261.36 per share, it is still trading 21.3% below its 52-week high of $332.28 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Texas Instruments’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,350.
